Owning an Ather

Ather vs petrol scooter: the five-year cost

An Ather costs more to buy than a 110 cc petrol scooter. The question is how quickly it earns that back. With petrol above ₹100 a litre in both Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, the answer for a daily commuter is: faster than you might think.

Updated 12 November 2026 · 2 min read · Pillai Auto, authorised Ather dealer

On this page

  1. Where the savings come from
  2. A worked example over five years
  3. What to weigh on the other side
  4. Our honest take

Where the savings come from

  1. Energy. About 24 paise per km on home electricity against roughly ₹2.30–2.40 per km in petrol. See the charging cost guide.
  2. Road tax. Tamil Nadu has extended its 100% motor vehicle tax exemption for electric vehicles until 31 December 2027. Puducherry has its own rules — see our registration guide.
  3. Servicing. No engine oil, oil filter, spark plug, air filter or clutch. Ather's own blog lists typical wear parts — brake pads from about ₹260, drive belts at 50,000 km — and the Konarc's sealed gearbox needs servicing just once a year.

A worked example over five years

For a commuter riding 1,000 km a month (60,000 km over five years) in Chennai:

Petrol scooterAther (home charging at ₹8/unit)
Fuel / electricity≈ ₹1,43,700≈ ₹14,400
Difference≈ ₹1,29,000 in the Ather's favour

This assumes petrol stays at ₹107.77 and a petrol scooter averages 45 km/l. It excludes servicing, where the Ather is also usually cheaper, and the purchase price, which varies by model.

What to weigh on the other side

  • Purchase price. Compare like for like — an Ather against a well-equipped petrol scooter, not the cheapest one.
  • Battery. The standard warranty covers 3 years / 30,000 km; extending it to up to 10 years / 1,00,000 km protects the biggest cost item. See the battery warranty guide.
  • Insurance. Comprehensive cover is needed for both; ask us for quotes on the model you choose.
  • How much you ride. The savings scale with kilometres. At 300 km a month, payback takes much longer than at 1,500.

Our honest take

For anyone riding 30 km or more a day, an Ather usually costs less over five years than a petrol scooter, even after the higher purchase price. For very light use, buy one because you prefer how it rides — not for the savings. Use our EMI calculator to see how the monthly payment compares with your current fuel spend.

Questions we get asked

For regular commuters, usually yes. At 1,000 km a month in Chennai, energy alone saves about ₹2,150 a month compared with a petrol scooter, before service savings.

Tamil Nadu has extended its 100% road tax exemption for electric vehicles until 31 December 2027.

Periodic inspections, brake pads, tyres and (on belt-driven models) a belt around 50,000 km. There is no engine oil, filter, spark plug or clutch.
